location.site: UMore Park, northeast portion / east of Dakota County Technical College
location.location_note: Official sources place the campus on a 280-acre parcel in UMore Park in Rosemount; no public street address or building-level parcel identifier was confirmed during this refresh.

evidence_grade: A-: official City of Rosemount, Minnesota PUC, Minnesota Governor, and Meta sources verify approval, active construction/development, project sponsor/entities, site, scale, and target operations/completion window; building-level permit/CO/energization records and current IT-load capacity remain unverified.
status_note: Rosemount's official development page says City Council approved Project Bigfoot/Jimnist for a technology campus/data center in UMore Park and to watch for early development. The same page, Governor's office, and Meta fact sheet place completion/operations in 2026. MPR reported on 2026-06-12 that Meta's Rosemount hyperscale data center was under construction, with an aerial image dated 2026-05-28. Rosemount Ordinance 2026-03, adopted 2026-04-21, imposed a citywide data-center moratorium but expressly exempts construction/expansion for existing or approved data center projects.

actions.access_caveat: PUC news release verifies the approved service agreements and interconnection-agreement category, but does not publish a MW amount in the release.
actions.evidence_note: PUC identified the data center as owned/operated by a Meta affiliate, Amber Kestral, LLC, in Rosemount on the northeast portion of UMore Park.

actions.action_type: official development-progress status / City Council approval narrative
actions.access_caveat: City page is an official narrative article, not the underlying resolution, packet, permit, or roll-call record.
actions.evidence_note: The city says Council approved Project Bigfoot, a Jimnist, LLC technology-campus/data-center proposal on 280 acres formerly owned by the University of Minnesota, with buildings totaling approximately 725,000 square feet.

actions.government_body: Office of Governor Tim Walz and Lt. Governor Peggy Flanagan
actions.access_caveat: Announcement is not a local permit or energization record.
actions.evidence_note: Governor's office announced Meta would build an $800 million, 715,000-square-foot data center on a 280-acre parcel in UMore Park, with about 100 operational jobs and at least 1,000 peak construction jobs.

actions.access_caveat: Company fact sheet; not a permit, inspection, service, or energization record.
actions.evidence_note: Meta lists $800M+ Minnesota data center investment, approximately 100 operational jobs once completed, 1,000 peak skilled trade workers, renewable-energy matching, and water-efficiency measures.

actions.result_status: adopted; approved/existing data center work exempted
actions.access_caveat: Moratorium ordinance is regulatory context, not a project milestone approval.
actions.evidence_note: The ordinance prohibits new data-center actions during the study period but allows construction/expansion of structures or equipment for existing or approved data center projects.

actions.access_caveat: Regional media observation; used only to corroborate physical construction because no city inspection/CO record was located.
actions.evidence_note: MPR identified Meta's Rosemount hyperscale data center as under construction and dated its aerial image May 28, 2026.

capacity_note: No current official MW/IT-load figure was located. The PUC release confirms approved electric-service and interconnection agreements but omits load. Secondary reporting from 2022 PUC filings described Amber Kestral as initially at least 10 MW and growing to exceed 75 MW over 10 years; that figure is not promoted to capacity_mw because an accessible official filing was not retrieved in this refresh.
owner: Meta Platforms, Inc.; PUC/customer affiliate: Amber Kestral, LLC; local application/development entity: Jimnist, LLC

Both are retained as scale evidence; no dedicated building_area_sqft field is added.
